page.layout: One column of running text, with no marginal notes. Left of the column is the edge of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed. Gathering signature at the foot below the text.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~12 letters] quae est Euangelium, seu historia Euangelica. 2. Scriptorem seu personam scribentis, quae fuit Marcus de quo vide B. Aretium in prolegomenis in Euangelium Marci.

Historiam Euangelicam describendi occasio priuata seu peculiaris Marco oblata fuit à fratribus Italicis & his quae Romae erant, quorum rogatu hunc libellum conscripsit. Rationes vero scribendi plures alias eum habuisse certum est: vt nimirum posteritas, fidei Christianae certam haberet historiam ex doctrina ipsius Christi. Et quia non Apostolus, sed sectator tantum Apostolorum fuit Marcus, sicuti & Lucas, obseruatione dignum est, nihil interesse ad percipiendum & praedicandum Euangelium, vtrum illi annuncient, qui eundem Dominum hic in carne apparentem, discipulatu famulante secuti sunt, an ij qui ex illis fideliter comperta tradiderunt.

p.i: Propositio & scopus est: Messiae vitam in his terris actam describere, mortem, resurrectionem & ascensum in coelos, vbi pro redemptis suis fidelibus manet intercessor vsque ad diem iudicij.

main_text.p: Potest hoc propositum isto syllogismo comprehendi:

p.i: Is in quo euenerunt ea quae in Christo euentura praedixerunt prophetae, est Christus.
Atqui Iesus hic Nazarenus, est is in quo illa euenerunt.

main_text.p: Huius syllogismi propositio confirmatur testimoniis prophetarum, quae passim in hac historia allegantur. Assumtio vero confirmatur

page.notes: The first line is Greek and is only partly legible in the scan (it looks like κειμένω ὕλλω or similar), so it is marked illegible. The running head has been normalised from SECVNDVM MARCVM to SECUNDUM MARCUM. The final sentence runs to the foot of the page and is not finished on this page, so the text ends with "confirmatur" and the continuation is on the next page. The Greek line is printed text, and its reading should be checked against the original. Some of the Latin italic lines show a special letter in "Nazarenus" that has been read as Z.
